User Story: How to read this sheet.
Expected Behavior: One row per discrete user-facing capability, grouped by Area. User Story is the intended outcome; Expected Behavior is what the code actually does (the primary source). Source Files cite the evidence (file or file:line). Filter out the (legend) rows to see only features.
Notes: Generated from source on 2026-06-21; spot-verified against https://organized-glitter-preview.up.railway.app/ with the e2e test account (both verticals enabled).

User Story: What each Status value means.
Expected Behavior: Documented (code) = behavior described from reading the source, not yet exercised live. Verified = the surface renders on the preview deployment (route loads, expected UI present); it does NOT assert every interaction was driven end-to-end. Issue found = a likely defect or inconsistency spotted while reading the code (suspicion, not preview-confirmed unless the note says so). Not implemented (web) = described in domain docs but absent from the web app.
Notes: A row can render fine yet still be flagged Issue found (e.g. META-016): the issue flag takes precedence in Status, and the rendering result is kept in Notes.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to sign in with my email and password so that I can access my collection.
Expected Behavior: AuthForm validates email format and password >=6 chars (Zod), then loginWithPassword normalizes the email, re-validates format, and calls pb.collection('users').authWithPassword. If the returned record is not verified it clears authStore and returns a verification-required error; on success PostHog logs AUTH_LOGIN_SUCCEEDED and navigates to the resolved redirect (default /overview). Already-authed visitors are bounced to the redirect via a useEffect.
Notes: Verified on preview: e2e creds log in and land on /overview. Login client schema requires only 6-char password while reset/change require 8+; unverified users are authenticated server-side first then explicitly cleared.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to sign in with Google or Discord so that I can skip password entry.
Expected Behavior: loginWithOAuth2 runs a connectivity check then calls pb.collection('users').authWithOAuth2 with the chosen provider via popup; on success it ensures beta_tester is set on the user, logs AUTH_LOGIN_SUCCEEDED, and navigates to the resolved redirect. Popup-blocked/cancelled/closed errors map to friendly messages.
Notes: Same handlers wired on both Login and Register pages; OAuth users get beta_tester=true auto-applied.

User Story: As a visitor, I want to create an account with email, username, and password so that I can start tracking projects.
Expected Behavior: AuthForm (Zod) requires a valid email, 3-20 char username matching [a-zA-Z0-9_-], password >=6, and matching confirmPassword. registerWithPassword re-checks password match, maps fields, creates the users record with beta_tester hard-coded true, then calls requestVerification. On success it shows a verification-sent toast and navigates to /email-confirmation with the email in state.
Notes: beta_tester is hard-coded true for every signup. No 8-char/complexity rule at registration (only 6-char min), unlike reset/change-password flows.

User Story: As a crafter, I want my email verified via the link I received so that my account is activated and I can log in.
Expected Behavior: VerifyEmail reads :token from the URL and on mount calls confirmEmailVerification, which calls pb.collection('users').confirmVerification(token). Missing token shows an invalid-link error; success shows a confirmation and auto-redirects to /login after 3s; token/expired errors are rewritten to a request-new-link message.
Notes: Route is /auth/verify-email/:token.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to resend my confirmation email so that I can verify my account if the first email was lost.
Expected Behavior: EmailConfirmation shows the address (from navigation state, or current auth store if authed) and a Resend button that calls requestVerification(email) -> pb.collection('users').requestVerification. Shows a sent toast on success. The display fallback ('your email') is separated from the resend value, and Resend is disabled and guarded when no real email can be resolved.
Notes: Fixed in PR #112 (merged): resend is disabled/guarded when no real email resolves, and the display fallback no longer leaks into the resend call, with regression coverage for the no-email and route-state paths. Previously, with no location state and an unauthenticated user, email defaulted to the literal string 'your email' and Resend called requestVerification('your email').

User Story: As a visitor, I want to request a password reset email so that I can regain access when I forget my password.
Expected Behavior: ForgotPassword validates the email is present and matches an email regex, then calls requestPasswordReset(email) -> pb.collection('users').requestPasswordReset. On success it switches to a 'check your email' confirmation state and toasts; errors are surfaced via toast.

User Story: As a visitor, I want to set a new password using my reset link so that I can sign in again.
Expected Behavior: ConfirmPasswordReset reads :token from the canonical HTTPS path, requires both password fields to match and pass validatePasswordStrength (>=8 chars, upper, lower, digit), then calls confirmPasswordReset(token, password, confirm) -> pb.collection('users').confirmPasswordReset. On success it shows a completion state and redirects to /login after 3s. The same URL is the iOS universal link and web fallback. Legacy query and hash routes preserve opaque token segments and redirect to the canonical route. Missing, invalid, expired, and reused tokens share the request-new-link recovery. Token path segments are redacted from analytics and exception context.
Notes: Fixed in PR #111 (merged): reset-confirmation errors are now preserved as Error instances before classification and matched case-insensitively, with a regression test for expired-token failures. Previously handleSubmit threw a string, so the err instanceof Error branch never matched and the page fell through to the generic message. INT-957 adds the shared web and native link contract.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to change my account password so that I can keep my account secure.
Expected Behavior: ChangePassword (auth-gated; redirects to /login if no user) requires current/new/confirm fields, that new matches confirm, that new differs from current, and that new passes validatePasswordStrength (8+ with upper/lower/digit). It calls changePassword -> pb.collection('users').update with oldPassword/password/passwordConfirm. On success it clears the form and, after 3s, calls signOut() and navigates to /login.
Notes: Forces re-login after success; maps PB 400/401/403/429 to specific error copy.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to request an email-address change so that I can update my contact email.
Expected Behavior: ChangeEmail (auth-gated) validates the new email is present, differs from current, matches an email regex, and is <=254 chars, then calls requestEmailChange(newEmail) -> pb.collection('users').requestEmailChange. On success it shows a confirmation-sent state; current email stays active until confirmed. Maps 400/429 to specific error copy.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to confirm my new email address with my password so that the change takes effect.
Expected Behavior: ConfirmEmailChange reads :token from the URL (missing token redirects to /login) and requires the current password, then calls confirmEmailChange(token, password) -> pb.collection('users').confirmEmailChange. On success it clears the form, toasts, and redirects to /login after 3s; maps 400/404/429 to specific error copy.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to permanently delete my account and data so that I can leave the service.
Expected Behavior: DeleteAccount (auth-gated) requires a confirmation checkbox and optional feedback notes. AccountDeletionService.deleteAccount verifies the current user matches, builds a usage snapshot across all owned collections, writes an audit record to account_deletions, then deletes the users record (404 treated as already_deleted). On success it calls signOut() and navigates to /. If the user delete fails after the audit was captured, a 'request captured but removal failed, contact support' error is returned.
Notes: Relies on PB cascade rules to remove related records; audit row created before the actual delete.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to log out so that my session is cleared on this device.
Expected Behavior: signOut (from AuthContext) guards against concurrent calls, clears local user state, calls authLogout (pb.authStore.clear) and queryClient.clear() to drop cached session data, and returns a success/error result. Even on error it still clears local state and the auth store.
Notes: queryClient.clear() prevents stale prior-session data after re-login.

User Story: As a crafter, I want app pages to require login so that my data stays private.
Expected Behavior: ProtectedLazyRoute wraps protected routes in ProtectedRoute, which reads useAuth; while isLoading or initial check is incomplete it shows a loading spinner, and if no user it redirects to /login passing the current location as state.from (so post-login redirect returns there via resolveAuthRedirectDestination). Session validity is derived from pb.authStore.isValid.
Notes: resolveAuthRedirectDestination sanitizes redirect targets (must start with single '/') to prevent open-redirect; default /overview.

Feature: Root-route handling for logged-in vs logged-out
User Story: As a visitor or crafter, I want the site root to show the right landing experience so that I reach the correct page for my auth state.
Expected Behavior: RootRoute ('/') shows a loading spinner until auth settles, then renders the unified Home page for all auth states (it does NOT redirect authenticated users). The 'redirect already-authed users away' behavior instead lives on /login and /register, whose useEffects navigate to the resolved redirect (default /overview) once auth is confirmed.
Notes: Unified-home design intent: '/' is the same Home for everyone; redirect-away logic is page-level on the auth forms.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to see all my diamond painting projects in one place so that I can browse my collection.
Expected Behavior: Dashboard renders the user's projects via useDashboardData -> useProjects against the PocketBase 'projects' collection, fetched in parallel with metadata as soon as userId is available. Returns paginated results (default page size 25 from FilterContext), default sort last_updated desc, with optimistic navigation data and scroll/highlight restoration on back navigation. Shows error banner on fetch failure and an empty state with a Clear Filters or Add New Project CTA when no results.
Notes: Service-layer default page size is 20 but only applies as a fallback; the dashboard passes FilterContext pageSize of 25. Verified on preview: /dashboard renders Projects list shell (diamond fixtures not seeded for test account).

User Story: As a crafter, I want to filter projects by their status so that I can focus on one part of my workflow.
Expected Behavior: Status filter defaults to 'everything' (no status clause). Selecting one of wishlist/purchased/stash/kitted/progress/onhold/completed/archived/destashed appends status = {:status} in projectQueryBuilder and resets page to 1. Rendered as a fluid segmented bar (desktop, with keyboard nav) or a popover (mobile) in DashboardStatusSegments, each segment showing a live count.
Notes: Verified on preview: /dashboard shows Browse by Status segments.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to filter projects by company so that I can see kits from a specific brand.
Expected Behavior: Company dropdown defaults to 'all' (no filter). Options come from MetadataContext.companies. Selecting a company maps to the PocketBase 'company' field and resets page to 1.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to filter projects by artist so that I can find pieces by a specific designer.
Expected Behavior: Artist dropdown defaults to 'all'. Options come from MetadataContext.artists. Selecting an artist maps to the 'artist' field and resets page to 1.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to filter projects by drill shape so that I can group round versus square kits.
Expected Behavior: Drill shape dropdown defaults to 'all' with hard-coded options Round and Square (values round/square). Maps to the 'drill_shape' field and resets page to 1.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to filter by the year I finished a project so that I can review a given year's completions.
Expected Behavior: Year finished dropdown defaults to 'all' with options loaded dynamically via useAvailableYears. Selecting a year filters date_completed between {year}-01-01 and {year}-12-31 and resets page to 1.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to filter projects by one or more tags so that I can find kits I've categorized.
Expected Behavior: Multi-select tag filter defaults to empty. Selecting multiple tag IDs builds an OR query over project_tags_via_project.tag. Deduplicates selections, shows a count badge, has a clear control, and resets page to 1. Renders as an inline panel on mobile and a popover on desktop.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to search my projects by text so that I can quickly find a specific kit.
Expected Behavior: Header search input commits after a 350ms debounce (useDeferredValue) with no client-side block, but toProjectFilterCriteria drops terms shorter than 2 characters (MIN_SEARCH_LENGTH), so a 1-char query returns unfiltered results. Default search is title-only.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to optionally search notes and source links so that I can find projects by content beyond the title.
Expected Behavior: searchAllFields defaults to false (title only). When enabled, the query builder performs a broader contains search across title, general_notes and source_url with OR logic. Toggling resets page to 1.

Feature: Include mini kits / destashed / archived toggles
User Story: As a crafter, I want to include or exclude mini, destashed, and archived kits so that I can control which projects appear.
Expected Behavior: includeMiniKits defaults to true; when false the query excludes kit_category = 'mini'. includeDestashed and includeArchived default to false (excluding those statuses) and are disabled unless the active status is 'everything'. Each toggle resets page to 1.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to clear all active filters at once so that I can reset to my full collection.
Expected Behavior: clearActiveFilters resets only narrowing filters (status to 'everything', company/artist/drill/year to 'all', flags to defaults, search to empty, tags to empty) while preserving sort, view type, page size and current page. Triggered from the ResultsSummaryBar Clear All link or the empty-state button.

User Story: As a crafter, I want one-click preset views so that I can jump to common slices of my collection.
Expected Behavior: DashboardQuickViews offers four presets: Waiting to arrive (purchased, sort date_purchased asc), Ready to start (kitted), In progress (progress, sort date_started desc), and Finished this year (completed + current year, sort date_finished desc). Selecting one applies a filter+sort patch and highlights the active view; a Clear quick view option appears when one is active.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to sort my projects by various fields so that I can order them meaningfully.
Expected Behavior: Sort defaults to last_updated desc. Valid fields: last_updated, date_purchased, date_finished, date_started, date_received, kit_name, company, artist, status, width, each asc or desc. SortSheet presents grouped options (Recent Activity, By Date, By Name, By Attribute) as a drawer (mobile) or sheet (desktop). The query builder applies nulls-last handling via _has_value segments and appends title as a tiebreaker. When sorting by a date field, projects missing that date are grouped under a 'No date' divider sized by useUndatedProjectCount.
Notes: No-date sort group counted by useUndatedProjectCount, rendered via useSortDividers.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to page through results and choose page size so that large collections stay manageable.
Expected Behavior: Default page size 25 with options 25/50/100; changing page size resets to page 1. Pagination shows Showing X-Y of Z, Previous/Next (disabled at boundaries) and numbered pages (max 5 desktop, 3 mobile) with ellipses. Any filter/sort change resets currentPage to 1. The next page is prefetched. totalItems may be an estimate (shown with a + suffix) when PocketBase's skipTotal optimization is active.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to switch between grid, list and table layouts so that I can view projects the way I prefer.
Expected Behavior: View type is grid, list or table, defaulting to list on phones and grid on tablet/desktop, persisted in localStorage 'dashboard-view-type' (validated on read). Grid shows responsive cards with thumbnail/title/metadata/status; list shows full-width rows; table (desktop only, sticky header, sortable columns) falls back to ProjectTableCard on mobile. Toggle fires a DASHBOARD_VIEW_TOGGLED analytics event.
Notes: List/grid/table all share sort-aware group dividers and a sort-dependent metadata line.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to see how many projects are in each status so that I can gauge my workflow at a glance.
Expected Behavior: DashboardStatusSegments displays per-status counts from useDashboardStatusCounts, which calls projectsService.getBatchStatusCounts (single getFullList query, batch 500, status field only, in-memory counting). Counts apply the same search/company/artist/tags/year/drill filters but skip the archived/destashed exclusion checkboxes; a virtual 'everything' total is computed. Counts show skeleton pulses while loading and are suppressed on error.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to create a new project with full details and a cover image so that I can track a new kit.
Expected Behavior: NewProject (routed via NewProjectRouter when the diamond vertical is enabled) renders ProjectFormSections with fields: title (required, max 255), status (default wishlist), company, artist (default round drill shape, full kit category), tags, dimensions, total diamonds, color count, 4 dates, source URL, general notes, and a croppable cover image. Validated client-side via ProjectFormSchema (zod). New company/artist names are created first via their mutations, then useCreateProject creates the 'projects' record and its optional cover image in one FormData request before linking tags. Create requests are not retried automatically because an interrupted response can leave the save outcome unknown; the user is told to check the project list before retrying. Partial tag failures show a warning, while successful creates redirect to the detail page. Image MIME rejections surface an IncompatibleImageDialog.
Notes: PR #121 adds authenticated E2E coverage proving diamond project color count survives create/edit round trips.

Feature: Project cover image upload and crop
User Story: As a crafter, I want to upload, crop and remove a cover image so that my project has an accurate thumbnail.
Expected Behavior: The form's cover image section accepts JPG/PNG/GIF/WebP/HEIC up to the IMAGE_MAX_FILE_SIZE limit (validated by schema), opens an ImageCropDialog (4:3 default, 1200x900 output, with presets) after selection, supports use-original, and allows removal (sets imageRemoved). The edit form compares File identity so crop output and consecutive replacements reach the save mutation. Removing clears imageFile/imageUrl. On the detail page, ProjectCoverImageEditor lets the user add/replace the cover in place: it normalizes, crops, compresses, and saves via useProjectUpdateUnified with a Cover image updated toast.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to view a project's full details so that I can review everything about a kit.
Expected Behavior: ProjectDetail fetches the project via useProjectDetailQuery (expands company, artist, tags with graceful fallback; 5-min stale time) and renders ProjectDetailView with hero image, title/company, a details meta panel, a 4-step purchase/received/started/completed timeline, general notes, and progress notes. Supports optimistic navigation data from the dashboard, shows ProjectNotFound after auth confirms a missing project, and a back button that restores dashboard filter context (or returns to the randomizer when entered from there).

User Story: As a crafter, I want to edit a project's fields so that I can keep its details accurate.
Expected Behavior: EditProject (full page) and ProjectEditDrawer (opened from the detail page Edit button) both render ProjectFormSections over the existing project, validate via ProjectFormSchema, and persist via the project update path. Nothing saves until Update is pressed; title is required. Optional update fields use three intents: omitted values stay unchanged, null clears the stored value, and concrete values replace it. Full-form clear controls preserve null through the command mapper and PocketBase FormData adapter. Field-level errors clear as the user edits changed fields, and image MIME rejection surfaces the IncompatibleImageDialog.
Notes: Two entry points: standalone /projects/:id/edit page and the in-place drawer from project detail.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to change a project's status from the detail view so that I can move it through my workflow.
Expected Behavior: StatusDropdown (pill or default variant) lets the user pick any of the nine statuses (wishlist, purchased, stash, kitted, progress, onhold, completed, archived, destashed). Selection calls useUpdateProjectStatus -> projectsService.update with an optimistic cache patch and rollback on error, fires PROJECT_STATUS_CHANGED, and shows a Status Updated toast. All status values (including mark-complete, on-hold, destash) flow through this one control.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to edit the purchase/received/started/completed dates inline so that I can correct the timeline without opening the full edit form.
Expected Behavior: The detail-view timeline renders a TimelineDateEditor per date field (Purchased, Received, Started, Completed) that updates that single date via the project detail dates mutation. Set steps show a filled marker; the mutation validates date order and a newly saved completion date marks an active project completed.
Notes: One row covers all four date fields; same inline editor reused per field.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to edit a project's general notes inline so that I can jot down details quickly.
Expected Behavior: ProjectNotes (inline variant) on the detail page saves general notes via useUpdateProjectNotesSectionMutation -> projectsService.update of the general_notes field; notes are capped at 5000 characters by the schema.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to add and remove tags on a project so that I can categorize my kits.
Expected Behavior: InlineTagManager optimistically updates its tag list and calls TagService for each add or remove. It rolls back failed writes, reports changes to the parent form, and relies on project-save synchronization as a fallback.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to add a dated progress note with an optional photo and caption so that I can document my progress.
Expected Behavior: ProjectProgressNotes opens a ProgressNoteDialog containing ProgressNoteForm: a date input, optional croppable image (4:3, 1200x900, with compression progress), and an optional rich-text caption. Submit calls useAddProgressNoteMutation -> ProgressNotesService.create against the 'progress_notes' collection, invalidates detail and progress-note queries, and shows a Progress note added toast.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to edit a progress note's caption so that I can fix or expand what I wrote.
Expected Behavior: ProgressNoteItem provides an inline edit mode (pencil action) with a RichTextEditor and Save/Cancel. Saving calls useUpdateProgressNoteMutation -> ProgressNotesService.updateContent for the note and invalidates project detail and progress-note queries.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to delete a progress note so that I can remove entries I no longer want.
Expected Behavior: ProgressNoteItem's trash action opens a confirm AlertDialog (wording adapts to whether the note has an image), then calls useDeleteProgressNoteMutation -> ProgressNotesService.delete and invalidates detail and progress-note queries (and the notes feed when no projectId is supplied).

User Story: As a crafter, I want to remove just the photo from a progress note so that I can keep the caption without the image.
Expected Behavior: Hovering a note image reveals a Remove image button that opens a confirm dialog and calls useDeleteProgressNoteImageMutation -> ProgressNotesService.removeImage (sets the image field to null), invalidating detail and progress-note queries.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to archive a project so that I can hide it from my main views without deleting it.
Expected Behavior: Archive is available from both the EditProject overflow menu and the ProjectDetailView actions menu. It calls useArchiveProjectMutation (sets status = 'archived' with an optimistic patch), invalidates lists and stats.overview, fires PROJECT_ARCHIVED, shows a Project Archived toast, and navigates to the dashboard.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to permanently delete a project so that I can remove kits I no longer track.
Expected Behavior: Delete is available from the EditProject overflow menu and the ProjectDetailView actions menu, each behind a confirm AlertDialog. useDeleteProjectMutation fetches the project, batch-deletes related progress notes and project tags, then deletes the 'projects' record (ownership verified fail-closed at the service), optimistically removes it from the list cache, invalidates lists/stats.overview/tags.stats, fires PROJECT_DELETED, shows a Project Deleted toast, and navigates to the dashboard.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to add a new coloring book with full bibliographic and acquisition details so that I can track it in my library.
Expected Behavior: NewColoringBook renders ColoringBookForm and on submit calls useCreateColoringBook with title, total_pages, status, series, theme, isbn, source_url, notes, edition, acquisition/lifecycle dates, publication_year, book_format, language, is_mystery, publisher, illustrator, cover_image, plus tag ids. On success it invalidates caches, toasts, and navigates to the new book detail. Validation requires a title and a whole-number page count from 1 through 500, checks URL/date/note constraints, and announces field errors as alerts.

Feature: Set publisher and illustrator on a book
User Story: As a crafter, I want to assign (and create) a publisher and illustrator so that I can attribute and filter my books.
Expected Behavior: The form offers publisher and illustrator selectors backed by useBookPublishers/useBookIllustrators (scoped to the user); new entries are created inline via useCreateBookPublisher/useCreateBookIllustrator. Detail view resolves names from the relation id, falling back to stored names.

Feature: Set total page count for a book
User Story: As a crafter, I want to specify how many pages a book has so that the app can generate trackable page records and compute progress.
Expected Behavior: Normal creation and increases require a whole-number page count from 1 through 500. Existing legacy books above 500 can keep their current total but cannot increase it. A reduction succeeds only when every page above the requested total is untouched; any worked page rejects the operation without deleting or hiding data. Direct updates can reduce at most 500 pages, while larger reductions use authenticated atomic batches of at most 500 pages.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to upload (and crop) a cover image so that my book is visually identifiable in the library.
Expected Behavior: coverImage is accepted as a File (nullable) on the form with a coverImageRemoved flag for edits; ColoringService.getCoverImageUrl builds a (optionally thumbnailed) cover URL used on cards, hero, table and list rows.

Feature: Mark a book as a mystery (is_mystery)
User Story: As a crafter, I want to flag a book as a mystery so that the app hides page subjects until I reveal them.
Expected Behavior: is_mystery is a boolean stored at the book level via the form. It is book-level metadata only; per-page reveal state is tracked separately on each page (revealed_subject/revealed_at). Library cards and the detail hero show a 'Mystery' chip based on book.isMystery.

Feature: View a coloring book detail page
User Story: As a crafter, I want a detail page for each book so that I can see its cover, metadata, progress, tags, notes and pages in one place.
Expected Behavior: ColoringBookDetail loads the book, its pages (sorted by page_number, perPage 500), and tags. It renders a hero (cover, title, metadata line, status, completion), a pages contact-sheet section, a metadata details grid (publisher, illustrator, series, theme, ISBN, publication year, edition, language, format, source link, purchased/received/started/completed dates), and a notes section. Shows a 'not found' state for missing books.
Notes: Verified on preview: coloring book detail renders hero + Tags + Pages sections.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to edit a book's fields so that I can keep its details accurate.
Expected Behavior: EditColoringBook (and an inline ColoringBookEditDrawer on the detail page) reuse ColoringBookForm with initialBook/coverUrl and persist via useSaveColoringBookEdit; on success it returns to the book detail. Individual fields (status, notes, tags) can also be edited inline from the detail page.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to delete a book so that I can remove ones I no longer track.
Expected Behavior: The detail actions bar offers a delete control wired to useDeleteColoringBook (ColoringService.deleteBook); on success the user is navigated back to the coloring dashboard. Deleting page records recomputes book metrics via PocketBase hooks.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to move a book through statuses (wishlist to destashed) so that I can reflect where it is in my collection.
Expected Behavior: Status options are Wishlist, Purchased, On Bookshelf (Not Started / in_stash), In progress, Completed, Archived, Destashed. Status can be set on create/edit and changed inline from the hero status popover (handleStatusChange -> useUpdateColoringBook). New books default server-side to status 'purchased' and ownership 'owned'.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to keep free-form notes on a book so that I can record context about it.
Expected Behavior: The detail page has a notes section that saves via useUpdateColoringBook (handleNotesSave). Notes are capped at 5000 characters by the form schema.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to add and remove custom tags on a book so that I can organize and filter my library.
Expected Behavior: Tags are managed on create (form tags), and inline on detail via ColoringBookTagManager (search existing or create new tag inline, remove with X). Saving calls ColoringTagService.syncBookTags and invalidates book/tag caches. Tag-sync failures surface a non-blocking warning toast (book still saves).

User Story: As a crafter, I want a dashboard listing all my coloring books so that I can see and open my collection.
Expected Behavior: The /coloring dashboard route redirects to /dashboard?craft=coloring, which renders ColoringDashboardPane fed by useColoringList. Books are shown via ColoringBookGrid/ColoringBookListRow or ColoringBooksTable, each showing cover, title, publisher/series, status badge and completion progress; an empty state appears when the library is empty or filters match nothing. The library paginates server-side (default 50, selectable 25/50/100) with page and pageSize in the URL so browser history, shared links, and new-tab navigation preserve the same result position. Changing a filter, search, sort, or page size resets to page 1. Every sort includes the record ID as a stable tie-breaker.
Notes: Verified on preview: /dashboard?craft=coloring renders the coloring pane with pagination.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to filter my books by status, publisher, illustrator, tags and mystery so that I can find a subset quickly.
Expected Behavior: ColoringFilterStrip provides multi-select filters for status, publisher, illustrator and tags, plus toggles for mystery-only, include-archived and include-destashed. Filters drive the list query in useColoringList.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to search books by title or author so that I can jump straight to a known book.
Expected Behavior: ColoringFilterStrip keeps local search text, debounces typed changes for 350ms, then calls updateSearch so the title/author query feeds useColoringList without submit or blur. A hydration guard suppresses typed input while a saved filter is being restored, so the user's keystrokes do not race with the rehydrated search value.
Notes: PR #121 / PR #119 fixes typed coloring search committing after debounce. PR #219 adds a hydration guard so typed input is not overwritten by a late rehydration. See docs/coloring-search-hydration.md.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to sort books and switch between grid, list and table views so that I can browse the way I prefer.
Expected Behavior: Sort options include date added, title, publisher, progress and last activity with an asc/desc toggle. View mode switches between grid (responsive cards), compact list rows, and a desktop-only sortable table (cover, book, status, format, publisher, pages/progress, latest activity).

Feature: Show mystery chip on library cards and hero
User Story: As a crafter, I want a clear mystery indicator on book cards and the detail hero so that I can tell at a glance which books are mysteries.
Expected Behavior: Cards and the detail hero render a 'Mystery' chip when book.isMystery is true. Per the mystery model, the chip reflects book-level metadata; real covers are still shown (the chip does not hide the cover).

Feature: Auto-generate page records for a book
User Story: As a crafter, I want page records created automatically from the page count so that every page is individually trackable.
Expected Behavior: On normal book creation or an allowed increase, the PocketBase hook generates missing coloring_pages through total_pages with status not_started. Reductions reject any excluded page with a non-default status, started or completed dates, reveal subject or date, mediums, photos, or a progress-note record, and identify the highest worked page. They delete only untouched excess pages in authenticated atomic batches of at most 500, lowering total_pages after each batch without synthesizing status or dates.

Feature: View the book's page contact sheet
User Story: As a crafter, I want a grid of all pages in a book so that I can see overall progress and jump to any page.
Expected Behavior: ColoringBookPagesSection renders pages sorted by page_number as a responsive ContactSheetCell grid. Each cell links to page detail and shows the page number plus status icon and edge color. Books above 500 pages load 500-page batches with Previous and Next controls and a truthful range, keeping every preserved legacy page reachable. Mystery books show a page-number and star watermark until reveal.
Notes: Verified on preview: book detail Pages contact-sheet section renders.

Feature: View a coloring page detail page
User Story: As a crafter, I want a detail page for an individual coloring page so that I can manage its status, dates, photos, mediums, notes and reveal in one place.
Expected Behavior: ColoringPageDetail loads the page and parent book and shows a header with prev/next page navigation, a photo section, and a command panel (status, lifecycle dates, mediums, mystery reveal). Shows a 'page not found' state when missing. If the loaded page does not belong to the route's book id, the page is treated as missing and the not-found state renders.
Notes: PR #121 includes authenticated E2E coverage for page/book mismatch rejection so cross-book page URLs do not render another book's page.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to set each page's status so that I can track progress per page.
Expected Behavior: Page status options are not_started, palette_chosen, in_progress, on_hold, completed. Changing status (useColoringPageStatusAction -> set-status command) optimistically updates and refreshes book progress without creating or clearing dates. Saving a nonempty completed_at marks the page completed; book completion metrics are recomputed from completed page counts.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to set or clear a page's started and completed dates so that I can record when I worked on it.
Expected Behavior: useColoringPageLifecycleDates provides draft inputs (formatted in the user's timezone) with save/clear for started_at and completed_at. Draft refs preserve an unsaved sibling date draft while saving the other date, and validation rejects completed dates before started dates before saving (set-started-date/set-completed-date commands).
Notes: PR #121 includes coverage for the fix from PR #100: saving one lifecycle date no longer wipes the other unsaved date draft.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to upload, crop, reorder and delete photos on a page so that I can document my colored result.
Expected Behavior: useColoringPagePhotoManager handles upload (with a crop dialog and use-original option), delete, and set-main (first photo is the main image). Commands map to PocketBase photos+/photos-/reorder; photo commands skip optimistic updates and refetch after settling.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to mark which mediums (pencils, markers, etc.) I used on a page so that I can record my materials.
Expected Behavior: useColoringPageMediumSelection toggles mediums on/off (set-mediums command) with optimistic update and rollback on failure; available mediums come from the user's medium catalog. A PocketBase request hook rejects attaching any medium not owned by the requesting user (IDOR guard), verifying only newly added ids on update.
Notes: PR #121 adds authenticated E2E coverage for the foreign-medium IDOR guard: another user's coloring medium is rejected while an owned medium still attaches.

User Story: As a crafter, I want dated progress notes (with optional images) on a page so that I can journal my work.
Expected Behavior: ColoringPageProgressNotes lists notes (newest first) and supports add (date + markdown content + optional image), edit content, delete note, and delete note image, backed by ColoringPageProgressNotesService. Notes are user-scoped and tied to a page; deleting a page removes its notes.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to reveal what a mystery page turned out to be so that the page shows its real subject and photo after I uncover it.
Expected Behavior: On mystery books, the page command panel offers a reveal flow (useColoringPageMysteryReveal): enter a subject and submit to set revealed_subject and revealed_at (reveal-mystery command); an existing reveal can be edited to another value. Reveal state is per page, distinct from the book-level is_mystery flag, and gates the contact-sheet from hiding the page.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to undo a page reveal so that I can hide a subject I revealed by mistake.
Expected Behavior: Revealed mystery pages show a 'Mark unrevealed' action that runs a clear-mystery-reveal command, clearing revealed_subject and revealed_at without recording a new reveal event, and returning the page to the unrevealed state (the contact sheet hides it again).
Notes: Fixed in PR #114 (merged): adds the clear-mystery-reveal page command wired to a 'Mark unrevealed' control, with CONTEXT.md docs and regression coverage. Previously no unreveal/clear-reveal path existed and a revealed page could only be edited to another non-empty subject.

Feature: Upload swatch photos for a page color reference
User Story: As a crafter, I want to upload photos of my color swatches so that I can record what colors I used on each page.
Expected Behavior: ColorReferenceSection (inside the page command panel below Mediums) exposes an upload control for swatch photos. Uploading calls useSaveColorReference -> ColorReferencesService.save with action 'photos', which submits files to the transactional color reference route. Photos are protected files requiring a file token. Empty references are removed automatically.

Feature: View swatch photo thumbnails and originals
User Story: As a crafter, I want to view my swatch photos as thumbnails and open the original so that I can check my color choices.
Expected Behavior: ColorReferenceViewer renders protected thumbnails (320x320f) from ColorReferencesService.urls and opens the full-size original on tap. Both thumbnail and original URLs require a file token.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to remove a swatch photo I no longer need so that I can keep my references clean.
Expected Behavior: Removing a swatch photo calls ColorReferencesService.save with action 'remove' and the filename. If the last photo is removed and notes are empty, the server deletes the reference record automatically.

Feature: Edit swatch notes on a page color reference
User Story: As a crafter, I want to add or edit plain-text notes on my color reference so that I can record color codes and brand details.
Expected Behavior: ColorReferenceSection includes a notes input. Saving calls ColorReferencesService.save with action 'notes', which includes baseline conflict detection. Conflict returns 409; the user can reload and retry.

User Story: As a crafter, I want archive import to restore swatch photos and notes so that my color references survive a backup/restore cycle.
Expected Behavior: Archive import restores color references via restoreArchivedColorReference, which calls ColorReferencesService.restore sequentially with resumable receipts (restoreKey + restoreOffset). Successful mutation responses include referenceId and addedPhotoCount. Receipt retries contribute zero additions. Partial failures preserve committed additions via PartialColorReferenceRestoreError.
Notes: Restore submits one sheet per transaction. See docs/color-codes-and-swatches.md for the full restore contract.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to manage my list of diamond painting companies so that I can attribute kits to their brands.
Expected Behavior: CompanyList renders CompanyPageHeader (add-company dialog with create mutation) and CompanyTable, which lists each company with website link and a live project-usage count that deep-links to a filtered dashboard. Each row has an inline edit dialog and a delete action guarded by an AlertDialog confirmation that warns the company is removed from associated projects.
Notes: One consolidated row covering list/create/edit/delete; UX identical pattern. Usage counts present. Delete uses confirm dialog. Verified on preview: /options/companies renders Company List.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to manage my list of artists so that I can attribute kits to their creators.
Expected Behavior: ArtistList renders ArtistPageHeader (add-artist dialog with client-side duplicate-name check before the create mutation) and ArtistTable for list/edit/delete. Mirrors the company management pattern.
Notes: Consolidated CRUD row. Add dialog performs case-insensitive client-side duplicate check. Artists have no website field (unlike companies). Verified on preview: /options/artists renders Artist List.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to create, color-code, edit and delete tags so that I can categorize my diamond projects.
Expected Behavior: TagTable lists diamond tags (vocabulary 'Diamond projects') with color swatch, hex value, usage count deep-linking to filtered dashboard, and created date. Diamond tags support inline edit (EditTagDialog) and delete behind an AlertDialog confirmation that warns the tag is removed from associated projects.
Notes: Usage counts present for diamond tags. Tags carry a color attribute. Verified on preview: /options/tags renders Tag List.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to see and delete coloring tags so that I can clean up my coloring taxonomy.
Expected Behavior: TagTable lists coloring tags with color and usage counts, deep-links to filtered coloring dashboard, exposes delete behind AlertDialog confirmation, calls useDeleteColoringTag, deletes related coloring_book_tags join records first, deletes the tag, then invalidates coloring tag and book caches. Coloring tags are still created/assigned from book tagging and are not edited inline in TagTable.
Notes: PR #121 / PR #119 fixed tag manager being read-only for coloring tags: delete is now available with associated-book cleanup and regression coverage; inline edit remains unavailable.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to manage coloring book publishers so that I can attribute books to their publishers.
Expected Behavior: BookPublisherList delegates to BookTaxonomyListTab(kind='publishers'), which lists publishers with name and website link, an add dialog, inline edit dialog (name + website), and a delete action behind an AlertDialog that notes existing books keep their records (only the taxonomy row is removed).
Notes: Consolidated CRUD. No usage count shown. Update/delete call service directly (not a dedicated mutation hook). Verified on preview: /options/publishers renders Book Publisher Management.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to manage coloring book illustrators so that I can attribute books to their illustrators.
Expected Behavior: BookIllustratorList delegates to BookTaxonomyListTab(kind='illustrators'), sharing the publisher UI but without a website field. Supports add, inline edit (name only), and delete behind an AlertDialog confirmation.
Notes: Consolidated CRUD; same component as publishers. No website column, no usage count. Verified on preview: /options/illustrators renders Book Illustrator Management.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to manage my coloring mediums (type, brand, color count, notes) so that I can record what supplies I use on pages.
Expected Behavior: ColoringMediumList shows a table of mediums (name, type label, brand, color count) with an add/edit dialog capturing name, type (from a fixed enum), brand, color count, and notes. Delete now opens an AlertDialog confirmation before mutating (deleteMedium.mutate(id) runs only on confirm; dialog closes after the mutation settles).
Notes: Fixed in PR #113 (merged): delete now routes through an AlertDialog confirmation, restoring parity with Company/Tag/BookTaxonomy; regression test proves Delete does not mutate until confirm. Previously delete fired immediately with no confirmation. No usage count shown. Verified on preview: /options/coloring-mediums renders Coloring medium management.

Feature: Spin the wheel and record a spin
User Story: As a crafter, I want to spin a wheel over my selected items so that the app picks what to work on next and remembers the pick.
Expected Behavior: RandomizerWheel animates numbered segments over the selected targets. Each selected target gets a sequential wheel number visible in both the wheel and the target list. On completion, handleSpinComplete records a randomizer_spins record (user, optional project link, title/company/artist, selected_projects array, and a versioned metadata snapshot) and surfaces the result in RandomizerResultPanel. The wheel announces the winning number for screen readers. Wheel click and keyboard activation share the same guarded action; a same-pool refresh failure cancels the active session and gates new spins but preserves the completed result and section draft.
Notes: Spin disabled unless >=1 target selected. Persists to randomizer_spins collection. PR #214 added pool identity scoping, cancellation lifecycle, accessibility announcements, and measurement refresh.

Feature: Switch randomizer mode (diamond / coloring book / coloring page)
User Story: As a crafter, I want to choose whether the wheel draws from diamond projects, coloring books, or coloring pages so that I can randomize the craft I want.
Expected Behavior: RandomizerCraftSelector (exported from RandomizerControlsPanel) switches mode among diamond, coloring-book, and coloring-page. Mode is normalized against the user's enabled verticals (falls back if a craft is disabled) and reflected in the URL; spin label and empty-state copy change per mode. RandomizerControlsPanel is now a separate component for status eligibility checkboxes.
Notes: Mode persisted to URL (?mode=). Disabled-vertical modes are coerced. Verified on preview: /randomizer renders Craft mode control.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to filter the randomizer pool by status so that the wheel only includes items in the states I care about.
Expected Behavior: RandomizerEligibility holds diamondStatuses, bookStatuses, and pageStatuses (plus an ownership field) read from and written to the URL. Changing filters re-queries the target pool via RandomizerTargetsService; a Reset/Loosen-filters action restores DEFAULT_RANDOMIZER_ELIGIBILITY.
Notes: Eligibility is status-only; the ownership field exists but is forced to default and dropped from URL. No tag filter. Verified on preview: /randomizer writes eligibility status filters to URL.

Feature: Select the target pool (toggle / all / none)
User Story: As a crafter, I want to choose exactly which items go on the wheel so that I can include or exclude specific projects before spinning.
Expected Behavior: RandomizerTargetSelector lists available targets with per-item toggles plus Select-all and Select-none actions. Each selected target displays its sequential wheel number. Selection is mirrored to the URL (?items=, with a sentinel for an explicitly empty selection) and defaults to all targets when none is specified. Targets support search filtering; hidden targets retain their selection and wheel number. Changing the selected pool cancels an active wheel spin; its old completion cannot publish a result.
Notes: Selection persisted to URL; legacy ?projects= param still honored for diamond mode. PR #214 added pool identity scoping so clearing and restoring the selection cancels the spin and allows a new pick.

Feature: Pick a random page from a chosen book
User Story: As a crafter, I want the randomizer to drill into a randomly picked coloring book and pick an unfinished page so that I get a concrete page to color.
Expected Behavior: When the spin result is a coloring_book, RandomizerResultPanel offers a page picker; pickRandomPageFromBook fetches that book's unfinished pages (statuses not_started/palette_chosen/in_progress/on_hold), randomly selects one, and records a scoped coloring-page spin. Book-to-page results and failures are announced; focus moves when the focused book action is replaced by its page result.
Notes: Shows an error if no unfinished pages match. Records a second randomizer_spins record in coloring-page mode. PR #214 added accessibility announcements for page-pick results.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to pick a section of the diamond project to work on so that I can plan a manageable chunk.
Expected Behavior: For a diamond result, DiamondSectionHelper offers two section-picking modes toggled by radio buttons. Size mode (DiamondSectionSizePicker): select preset section sizes (3x3, 4x4, 5x5) or enter custom cm dimensions, then roll to estimate diamond count from the project's total dimensions. Multiple presets can be selected; the roll picks one at random. Number mode (NumberSectionPicker): enter section numbers separated by commas and pick one at random. Both modes persist the section into the spin's metadata via updateSpinMetadata. Unsaved size presets and number lists survive switching between modes. Refreshed project measurements update section estimates without resetting an unchanged selection.
Notes: Section kind is a discriminated union (size or number) in RandomizerSection. Section draft feeds the default diamond progress-note text. PR #214 added measurement refresh without selection reset.

Feature: Save a progress note from the diamond result
User Story: As a crafter, I want to save a progress note on the picked diamond project so that I log that the randomizer sent me to work on it.
Expected Behavior: For a diamond_project result, RandomizerResultPanel exposes a progress-note composer prefilled with a default (project title plus any section estimate); saveDiamondProgressNote writes a progress note to the project dated in the user's timezone.
Notes: Optional; saving the spin does not require a note.

Feature: Save a randomizer note on the picked coloring page
User Story: As a crafter, I want to save a note on the coloring page the randomizer picked so that I record activity against that page.
Expected Behavior: When the result is a coloring_page, saveRandomizerNote adds a coloring-page progress note (default text references the picked page) to the page identified in the target metadata.
Notes: Separate path from the diamond progress note (canSaveRandomizerNote gates on coloring_page result).

User Story: As a crafter, I want to pin a chosen item as my Next Up so that I remember what to work on next per craft.
Expected Behavior: RandomizerNextUpPanel shows the saved Next Up target for the active mode; toggleNextUpTarget pins/unpins the current result and clearNextUpTarget removes it. Preferences are stored per mode in user dashboard settings (randomizer_next_up).
Notes: Persisted to user_dashboard_settings.randomizer_next_up; one slot per mode.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to see my recent randomizer spins so that I can review what the wheel has picked.
Expected Behavior: SpinHistory lists prior spins from the randomizer_spins collection (filtered to the user's enabled crafts), shown inside a collapsible accordion below the wheel and result panels.
Notes: Total spin count also surfaced in stats.recentSpins.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to switch stats between crafts and between a specific year and all-time so that I can focus my analysis.
Expected Behavior: Stats page has a StatsScopeControl (all / diamond / coloring, gated to enabled verticals) and a StatsTimeScopeControl that toggles between a selected year and all-time; year options are derived from the user's yearly completion data plus the current year (max 5).
Notes: Scope falls back when a vertical is disabled. All-Crafts is composed client-side from diamond+coloring responses. Verified on preview: /stats renders scope with Diamond + Coloring regions.

User Story: As a crafter, I want a lead completion number and chart for my diamond paintings so that I can see how many I finish over time.
Expected Behavior: DiamondRegion shows a lead 'completed this year/all time' figure with prior-year totals and a LeadCompletionChart rendering monthly points (with previous-year comparison) for a year scope or yearly points for all-time, sourced from the diamond completions endpoints.
Notes: Backed by /api/stats/completions and /completions/yearly. Math lives server-side per stats-spec.md. Verified on preview: /stats Diamond paintings region renders.

User Story: As a crafter, I want library counts and typical timing metrics for my diamond kits so that I understand my stash and pace.
Expected Behavior: DiamondRegion renders a Library column (total kits, wishlist, in stash, kitted up, in progress, on hold, completed for the scope) and a Typical timing column (avg time in stash, time to start, time to finish, most common size/company/drill shape).
Notes: Backed by /api/stats/summary and /completion-times.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to see which companies, artists, tags, and sizes dominate my diamond collection so that I understand its composition.
Expected Behavior: MostRepresentedList in DiamondRegion shows top companies, artists, tags, and size buckets with server-provided totals and an 'Other' count (top lists fixed at 10).
Notes: Backed by /api/stats/collection.

User Story: As a crafter, I want a lead completion number and chart for my coloring pages so that I can see my coloring output over time.
Expected Behavior: ColoringRegion mirrors the diamond lead report for coloring pages (teal accent), showing completed-pages figure and a monthly/yearly completion chart from the coloring completions endpoints.
Notes: Backed by /api/stats/coloring/completions and /coloring/completions/yearly. Verified on preview: /stats Coloring region renders.

User Story: As a crafter, I want library counts and timing metrics for my coloring books/pages so that I understand my coloring collection and pace.
Expected Behavior: ColoringRegion renders a Library column (total books, active right now, active pages, finished books, wishlist) and a Typical timing column (avg page completion time, avg time before starting the first page, most common publisher/medium).
Notes: Backed by /api/stats/coloring/summary and /coloring/completion-times. Finished books falls back to bookStatusSplit when summary missing.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to see top publishers, illustrators, mediums, and tags so that I understand my coloring collection's composition.
Expected Behavior: ColoringRegion's MostRepresentedList shows top publishers, illustrators, mediums, and tags with server-provided totals and Other counts (top lists fixed at 10).
Notes: Backed by /api/stats/coloring/collection.

User Story: As a crafter, I want a single feed of my in-progress diamond projects and coloring pages so that I can quickly resume active work.
Expected Behavior: Overview fetches a combined feed via useOverviewData/OverviewService, filters to renderable items (diamond-project and coloring-page kinds), and renders them in OverviewActivityList with status/activity labels and links.
Notes: Aggregates across both crafts client-side; respects enabled verticals. Latest-note activity uses one minimal server query per active target under bounded concurrency, so transferred rows do not grow with note history. Verified on preview: /overview shows Welcome back + In progress feed.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to filter the overview by craft and sort it so that I can organize my active work my way.
Expected Behavior: OverviewCraftTabs filter the feed (all/diamond/coloring, with fallback when a vertical is disabled) and OverviewSortControl sorts by recent/oldest activity or name A-Z/Z-A; both selections persist to localStorage.
Notes: Persisted under og.overview.activeCraftFilter and og.overview.activeSort.

User Story: As a crafter, I want at-a-glance counts of active work and recent completions so that I see momentum without scrolling the feed.
Expected Behavior: OverviewRightRail renders the OverviewSnapshot: diamondActiveCount, coloringPageInProgressCount, and completedThisMonthCount, computed server-side over the current calendar month.
Notes: completedThisMonth uses a current-month date range. Verified on preview: /overview right rail snapshot renders.

User Story: As a crafter, I want one chronological feed of progress notes across my projects and coloring pages so that I can review my crafting journal in one place.
Expected Behavior: NotesFeedPage uses useNotesFeed to pull a paginated, cross-craft notes feed, flattens and re-sorts items by date then createdAt then id, groups them by month, and renders a NotesTimeline with Load-more pagination.
Notes: The merged infinite query uses per-source keyset cursors and retained overflow buffers. Each note row transfers once, and date/createdAt/id ordering stays deterministic across craft ties. Verified on preview: /notes renders month-grouped timeline (June/May 2026). PR #121 adds authenticated E2E coverage for the notes timeline with seeded diamond and coloring notes, verifying month grouping and cross-craft ordering.

Feature: Filter feed by craft / year / source
User Story: As a crafter, I want to narrow the notes feed by craft, year, and a specific project/book so that I can find relevant notes.
Expected Behavior: NotesFeedFilters provide a craft tab (all/diamond/coloring, coerced to available verticals), a year filter, and a source filter built from the loaded items; changing craft resets the source selection.
Notes: Source list derived from currently loaded items, sorted by title.

Feature: Add a progress note from the feed
User Story: As a crafter, I want to add a note directly from the notes page so that I can log progress without navigating to a project.
Expected Behavior: AddNoteCTA opens a composer; when the diamond tab has a specific source selected, it builds a direct ProgressNoteDialogTarget for that project so the note attaches without an extra picker step.
Notes: Direct composer target only for diamond source selections; otherwise general composer.

Feature: Timed work sessions / timer (not implemented in web)
User Story: As a crafter, I want to run a timer for a crafting session attached to a project or coloring page and optionally save a progress note so that I can track time spent.
Expected Behavior: Per CONTEXT.md, a work session is timed crafting activity recorded against a progress unit (diamond sessions attach to a Project, coloring sessions to a Coloring page), stored as individual session entries from which totals derive, with an optional progress-note companion at stop/save. No web implementation exists.
Notes: NOT implemented in web: no work_sessions collection (only randomizer_spins), no service/hook/UI. CONTEXT.md routes the full timer spec to docs/mobile/mobile-v1-scope.md, indicating mobile-v1 scope.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to enable or disable the diamond painting and coloring book trackers so that my navigation and dashboard only show the hobbies I use.
Expected Behavior: Two autosaving switches on the Profile > Preferences tab toggle diamond_painting and coloring_books. Toggling optimistically updates and persists via useSaveVerticalToggles; the app refuses to persist a state where both are off, blocking the switch and showing inline 'Pick at least one tracker.' copy. Captures a VERTICAL_PREFERENCES_UPDATED analytics event.
Notes: useEnabledVerticals silently falls back to DEFAULT_VERTICAL_TOGGLES when persisted data has both off, so a stale/both-off server state resolves to defaults rather than erroring.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to choose light, dark, or system appearance so that the app matches my visual preference across devices.
Expected Behavior: Profile > Preferences > Appearance shows a system/light/dark segmented control. Light uses Berry Cream; Dark uses Berry Cream after dark (deep navy stage with raspberry actions and lavender accent). System follows the device appearance. Selecting a theme optimistically applies it via next-themes and persists themePreference through useUpdateThemePreferenceMutation; on save failure it rolls back to the last server value. ThemeClassSync/AccountThemeSync apply the saved theme on load and map legacy Catppuccin preferences to Light or Dark.
Notes: Theme is account-level (synced across devices), not just a local toggle.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to set my account timezone so that project dates and stats display in my local time.
Expected Behavior: Profile > Preferences > Appearance includes a timezone selector that persists via useUpdateTimezoneMutation; failures surface an error toast and re-throw for the component to handle.

User Story: As a crafter, I want a single page linking to my companies, artists, tags, publishers, illustrators, and coloring mediums so that I can curate the dropdown values used across my projects.
Expected Behavior: The /options page renders grouped links under 'Diamond painting' (Companies, Artists, Tags) and 'Coloring' (Publishers, Illustrators, Coloring mediums). Groups are filtered by the user's enabled verticals, so a disabled vertical's list links are hidden.
Notes: Page title is 'Manage Lists'. Individual list editors (ArtistList, TagList, etc.) are the META-* rows. Verified on preview: /options renders Manage Lists with both vertical groups.

Feature: Account identity (avatar, username, email, password, danger zone)
User Story: As a crafter, I want to manage my avatar, username, email, password, and account deletion so that I control my identity and credentials.
Expected Behavior: Profile > Account tab shows avatar (editable via AvatarManager, upload or revert-to-initials), username (inline edit dialog that checks availability and calls UsersService.update), read-only email with a Change link, a Password row linking to /change-password, verification/beta/created-at status, and a danger zone. Email/password/delete are handled on dedicated pages.
Notes: Avatar update refetches profile and toasts; initials revert uses useAvatar hook.

Feature: Profile route and tabbed settings shell
User Story: As a crafter, I want my settings organized into Account, Preferences, Data, and Support tabs so that I can find a given setting quickly.
Expected Behavior: /profile renders a tabbed shell. Tab state is driven by the ?tab query param: 'preferences' is default (no param), 'account', 'data', 'support' map directly, and legacy ?tab=profile redirects to 'account'. Changing tabs updates the URL.
Notes: 'Settings' nav label points to /profile.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to download a CSV template, fill in diamond projects, and import the file so that I can bulk-add projects without manual entry.
Expected Behavior: The Data tab's Import region offers a template download (downloadCSVTemplate), file selection, and import. importProjectsFromCSV parses rows, maps each via mapParsedProjectToCreateDTO with validateProjectData (correcting/validating drill shape, status, dates, etc.), creates projects, and reports a result summary with imported/failed/skipped counts, validation issues, and tag warnings. A step rail and progress bar track the flow.
Notes: Photos cannot be imported via CSV; UI directs users to the separate Photos import afterward. Verified on preview: /profile?tab=data renders Import region. PR #121 covers the Data tab's format chips in both light and dark themes, guarding the import/export surface against the FormatChip contrast regression fixed in the release.

Feature: Diamond Art Club (DAC) order CSV import
User Story: As a crafter, I want to import my Diamond Art Club order export so that my purchased kits become projects without re-typing them.
Expected Behavior: Selecting a DAC CSV runs parseDacCsvFile to produce a preview (projects parsed, rows skipped, duplicates, first titles, warnings) before import. Importing calls importDacProjectsFromCSV, creating projects and showing a result summary. Includes a link to the DAC Orders page and notes DAC CSVs contain no photos.
Notes: Distinct from the Organized Glitter CSV path; preview is required and Import is disabled until projectCount > 0.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to upload a ZIP or folder of images and match them to projects/books/pages so that I can attach covers and progress photos in bulk.
Expected Behavior: Photos import accepts a .zip (analyzeZipFile) or a directory selection (analyzeFileList via webkitdirectory). Files are auto-matched to library records with a confidence level; a review table/cards let the user set target type, target record, and include/exclude per row. Cover overwrites are blocked unless explicitly allowed. Importing confirmed rows reports imported/skipped/failed counts, progress notes created, and overwrites.
Notes: Target types span diamond project cover/progress note and coloring book cover, page photo, and page progress note.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to export a single ZIP of all my data and photos so that I have a complete portable backup.
Expected Behavior: The Export region's 'Export full archive' builds a schema-version-2 .zip containing CSV data plus supported photos for diamond projects, progress notes, coloring books, coloring pages, and swatch photos (useDataArchiveExport). Schema version 2 adds colorReference per page (notes, photo paths). Export and import share a 512MB compressed ZIP ceiling; photos that would push the archive over that ceiling are omitted with an archive-size-limit warning and pruned from the manifest so the backup stays restorable. Protected swatch downloads use a file token session (fileTokenSession.ts) that refreshes the short-lived PocketBase token during long exports and retries authorization failures, so later swatches are not silently dropped when the original two-minute token expires. Shows a progress bar and a result alert with filename and any per-photo warnings (skipped or size-limited files).
Notes: PR #222 added 512MB ceiling, file token refresh, and photo budget tracking.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to restore data from an Organized Glitter archive ZIP so that I can recover or migrate my library into this account.
Expected Behavior: The Restore region accepts a previously exported .zip (rejected above the 512MB ceiling before reading entries) and runs useDataArchiveImport/importArchive, creating new records in the current account and skipping duplicates where it can match them. Schema versions 1 and 2 are both importable. Legacy coloring books above 500 pages are supported without an arbitrary maximum when the archive has complete unique page coverage; the authenticated restore route creates at most 100 generated pages per request. Schema-version-2 archives restore swatch photos one per transactional call (action restore) with restoreKey/restoreOffset for idempotent retry. Color reference restore uses PartialColorReferenceRestoreError to track committed swatch additions when a later photo transaction fails; additions already committed by earlier transactions stay in the photo summary so a retry can continue from receipts. Diamond projects from the same archive are kept distinct even when they share a title and source URL; recovery checkpoints preserve each archive ref's destination across retries and existing account records are matched at most once per restore. Same-account restores are serialized in the browser so overlapping restores cannot create duplicate records. The result alert reports created, matched, skipped, warning, and error totals with an expandable paginated error list (batches of 100).
Notes: Verified on preview: /profile?tab=data renders Restore archive region. PR #257 added distinct project preservation and recovery checkpoints.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to export just my data as CSV per category so that I can analyze it in a spreadsheet without downloading photos.
Expected Behavior: The Export region offers three CSV-only downloads: Diamond projects CSV, Coloring books CSV, and Coloring pages CSV, each via useLibraryCsvExport with a per-target loading state.
Notes: Three export targets share one hook.

User Story: As a crafter, I want a one-time welcome walkthrough so that I understand how to use the coloring tracker when I first sign in.
Expected Behavior: ColoringWalkthroughGate opens ColoringWalkthroughDialog once per account, only after auth is ready, when users.coloring_walkthrough_seen !== true and the user is on /overview or /dashboard. Closing/marking seen persists the flag so it does not reappear.

User Story: As a crafter, I want the app to tell me when I lose connectivity so that I understand why actions may not work.
Expected Behavior: useConnectionRecovery tracks browser connectivity and verifies the configured PocketBase health endpoint before dismissing the offline overlay. Check connection keeps the mounted app and unsaved form input in place; it does not reload, save drafts, or replay writes.
Notes: Recovery uses a five-second bounded no-store health check. Browser online/offline events only hint the automatic overlay path; an explicit Check connection always makes that request, even if navigator.onLine is still false. Failed checks keep the overlay open and explain that unsaved changes can still be lost by refreshing or closing the app.

User Story: As a crafter, I want the app installed as a PWA to keep working and auto-update so that I get a fast, app-like experience.
Expected Behavior: App registers the vite-plugin-pwa service worker (autoUpdate, immediate) on mount and triggers an update check on registration; main.tsx complements the reload-on-activation lifecycle. The health endpoint uses NetworkOnly caching.
Notes: Service worker registration is best-effort and silently degrades if unavailable. Cached app assets do not provide durable draft storage or offline write support.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to install Organized Glitter to my device so that I can launch it like a native app.
Expected Behavior: usePWAInstall captures beforeinstallprompt, detects installed/standalone state, and gates a prompt behind a 3s interaction delay with a 7-day dismissal stored in localStorage. macOS Safari gets manual install guidance. Profile > Support exposes an 'Install Web App' action that opens InstallAppDialog.

Feature: Navigation model (site header, bottom nav, account menu)
User Story: As a crafter, I want consistent navigation that adapts to my login state, device, and enabled hobbies so that I only see relevant destinations.
Expected Behavior: SiteHeader shows full APP_NAV_ITEMS and an account menu only when logged in; on Login/Register pages logged-out users see just the theme toggle, otherwise Login/Register buttons. BottomNavigation (phone) shows Overview/Dashboard plus a centered Add button gated on having at least one enabled vertical, and its add options are filtered by enabled verticals.
Notes: Add button hidden while verticals load or when both are disabled.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to send feedback from within the app so that I can report issues or ideas easily.
Expected Behavior: FeedbackDialog (opened from Profile > Support via useAccountMenuActions.handleFeedback) collects a message (10-5000 chars), optional name, and optional email. Submit calls sendFeedbackEmail in src/lib/feedback-email-service.ts, which validates input client-side, then posts with the signed-in user token to PocketBase POST /api/organized-glitter/feedback. The PocketBase hook requires a verified user, derives account identity from the session, limits each account to five attempts per 15 minutes, and sends through its configured SMTP mail client. On eligible API failures, the service opens a prefilled mailto to contact@organizedglitter.app but reports failure so the dialog stays open. Client validation, auth, rate-limit, and server failures skip the mailto fallback. Local development logs the message instead of calling the API.
Notes: The active route is on PocketBase; the Railway /api/send-feedback route remains only for legacy direct callers. Rate-limit retryAfter is returned in seconds. A controlled production message reached contact@organizedglitter.app on 2026-09-25.

User Story: As a crafter, I want to leave an optional tip so that the app stays free and maintained.
Expected Behavior: Settings > Support, the account menus, and the footer link to /support when tips are configured. /support explains what tips cover and links to Stripe-hosted Payment Links for $2, $3, $5, $10, or a custom amount. Stripe redirects to /support/success, a thank-you page that links back to the app.
Notes: SupportSuccess is a static confirmation page (no payment verification). Tips hide when no VITE_STRIPE_TIP_*_URL is set.

User Story: As a visitor, I want a marketing home page describing the app so that I can decide to sign up.
Expected Behavior: RootRoute waits for the auth check, then renders the Home marketing page (HomeHero, TwoCraftsSplit, ScrapbookFeatures, SarahSignature) with SEO metadata. The same unified marketing body is shown regardless of auth state; only SiteHeader differs by login state.
Notes: Per project convention, there is no auth-based content split on the home/marketing body.

User Story: As a visitor, I want an About page so that I understand who built the app and why.
Expected Behavior: /about renders a static marketing page with the app's backstory and contact links (Instagram, email) and sets SEO title/description/canonical metadata.

User Story: As a visitor, I want a privacy policy so that I know how my data is handled.
Expected Behavior: /privacy renders a static privacy policy with SEO metadata, stating data is not sold and describing collection, use, and user controls.

User Story: As a visitor, I want terms of service so that I understand the rules of using the app.
Expected Behavior: /terms renders numbered terms sections (acceptance, description, etc.) as static content with SEO metadata.

User Story: As a visitor, I want a link-in-bio page so that I can find Sarah's app, content, and social links from social media.
Expected Behavior: /links renders a link-in-bio style page with a profile header, a featured 'Try Organized Glitter' card, curated content/affiliate links, and Instagram, with social-share metadata (OG image, title, description). The page uses the public utility register (html.utility-register) so the product page atmosphere does not show; the app shell stays an opaque background fill with flat semantic styling.
Notes: Per PRODUCT.md, /links is brand public utility chrome, not a user-profile feature. Uses System as default for new visitors; both palettes use semantic tokens. No glass, paper, gradients, or Caveat.

User Story: As a visitor, I want a clear 404 page so that I can get back to the app when I hit a bad link.
Expected Behavior: NotFound renders a 404 page with a 'Back to Home' link and logs the attempted route (pathname, search, hash, user agent) for diagnostics.

User Story: As a visitor, I want a check-your-email page after signing up so that I know to verify my address and can resend the email.
Expected Behavior: EmailConfirmation shows a 'Check your email' landing that derives the address from navigation state, lets the user resend verification (requestVerification), and is marked noindex for search engines.
Notes: Auth-flow landing; see AUTH-050 for the resend-email behavior (resend guarded when no email resolves; fixed in PR #112).
